name: Medina Steps
summary: A stepped square minaret joins a quiet prayer hall, with open arches cut through warm ivory walls.
why: The stepped tower and low flat roof recall the architectural language of the Maghreb without copying a particular building. The continuous silhouette makes a complete mosque; two generous open arches keep the hall welcoming and readable.
risk: The identity is regional and architectural. The small tower opening is a secondary detail at launcher size.
reasonToChoose: A mosque rooted in North African architectural character should lead.
